Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd Reports Steady Output and Revenue Growth in Latest Results

LUSAKA – Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd, one of Zambia’s leading copper processors, posted steady production and revenue growth for the recent quarter, highlighting the continued resilience and importance of the copper sector to the country’s economy.

In financial results released Tuesday, Chambishi Copper Smelter reported copper cathode output of 58,900 tonnes for the quarter ended March 31, up 4.2% from 56,550 tonnes a year earlier. The company’s revenues rose to $427 million, a 5.1% increase on the back of firmer global copper prices and improved operational efficiencies.

"We are pleased with the operational performance this quarter, which reflects our ongoing investments in efficiency and sustainability," said General Manager Joseph Mulenga in a statement. "We continue to prioritize safety, environmental stewardship, and partnerships with local suppliers."

The company noted that operating costs remained broadly stable despite inflationary pressures, as procurement strategies and energy management initiatives helped offset rising fuel and input expenses. Gross profit for the quarter reached $70 million, compared to $66 million in the same period last year.

Industry observers say Chambishi Copper Smelter’s performance mirrors broader trends in Zambia’s mining sector, which has seen a moderate boost from higher copper prices fueled by global demand for green technologies.

"The results from Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd are encouraging and demonstrate the company’s focus on operational discipline," said Daniel Zulu, an analyst at Lusaka Securities Advisory. "Copper remains a pillar of Zambia’s export earnings, and sustained output from major smelters is vital for the sector’s stability."

The company’s workforce comprised 1,120 permanent employees at the end of the quarter, with an additional 340 contract workers. Chambishi Copper Smelter underscored its commitment to local employment and ongoing training programs, including the recent launch of a technical apprenticeship initiative in partnership with the Copperbelt Training Institute.

Looking ahead, the company said it would continue to invest in plant modernization and emission reduction projects. No major operational disruptions or supply chain issues were reported during the quarter.

"Our outlook remains positive, and we are focused on delivering value to our stakeholders and supporting the Zambian economy," Mulenga added.

Shares in parent company Luangwa Metals Holding rose 1.6% on the Lusaka Stock Exchange following the earnings release.
